svg.text: From the ventilator to the arterial trace: five links, and what breaks each one

g.text: The ventilator delivers a tidal volume
A cyclic, reproducible, machine-controlled stimulus of known size and timing
Some of that pressure reaches the pleural space
The fraction transmitted is set by lung stiffness relative to chest wall stiffness
Pleural pressure changes transmural pressure on the great veins and both ventricles
RV filling falls, RV afterload rises, and two to four beats later LV filling falls
Stroke volume swings, but only if the ventricles are on the steep limb
The size of the swing is the slope of the function curve at the operating point
The swing in stroke volume appears as a swing in pulse pressure
Requires stable arterial compliance across the cycle and a faithful pressure trace
spontaneous effort, a triggered breath, an arrhythmia
low tidal volume, stiff lung, open chest, tense abdomen
too few beats per breath, right ventricular failure
vasopressor or vasodilator moving the operating point

svg.text: Every condition that invalidates the measurement is a break in one of these links, not a separate rule.
Naming the link tells you the direction of the error and which alternative test escapes it.
